newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING - KNAUSS READY TO ENJOY CHRISTMAS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING - KNAUSS READY TO ENJOY CHRISTMAS.

text.p: If everything goes according to plan for Hans Knauss on Sunday, he could be heading home to Austria for Christmas with his second World Cup skiing win in a week and a healthy overall lead.
The good cheer may be limited to Austrians, however.

Italians will have very little to shout about when Alta Badia's daunting giant slalom, the last race before the Christmas break, brings to an end a gruelling week for the all-rounders on the men's Alpine skiing circuit.
This year, for the first time in a decade, the biggest attraction in the sport will be missing.
Alberto Tomba, Italy's triple Olympic and double world champion, has decided to skip the race after making his season's debut in a slalom at Madonna di Campiglio on Tuesday.

Tomba, who suffered a knee and wrist injury in training before the season started, decided to miss Alta Badia - one of the most difficult and demanding of giant slaloms - to keep to his training schedule.
The absence of "La Bomba", who has won here four times and been on the podium every year that the race has been held since 1986, is something of a calamity for the organisers.
When Tomba is in action, around 10,000 fans make their way to the remote resort in north-eastern Italy where their idol won his first ever podium place in 1986.
When he is not, half that number turn up and the noise levels at the finish are noticeably lower.

Tomba's participation, after his remarkable second place on Tuesday, would have brought acres of publicity -- preferably of a different kind to last season when he lobbed his heavy glass trophy and champagne magnum at a photographer.
In his absence, the focus is on Knauss - who won a super-giant slalom at Val d'Isere on Monday and who also took last year's giant in Alta Badia, his first World Cup win.
The Austrian has yet to win a giant this season, finishing third in Breckenridge and second in Park City in November.

Knauss, as an all-rounder, may have a slight disadavantage over some of his rivals since he arrives in Alta Badia after two downhills -- necessary to pile on the overall World Cup points -- in Val Gardena on Friday and Saturday.
Sweden's Fredrik Nyberg, winner of the last giant slalom in Breckenridge, is missing Saturday's downhill to concentrate on a race where he has never stepped on to the podium.
Swiss Steve Locher, winner here in 1993, is also a front-runner after his season-opening victory in the giant on the glacier at Solden in Austria on October 27.
Compatriot Michael Von Gruenigen is another, having chalked up a second and a third place so far this season.
The steep and icy Gran Risa piste is slightly longer than before with a few extra metres on the upper part.
